URL: https://abcnews.com/International/wireStory/iran-received-official-us-response-latest-offer-ending-136882729
ABC News (Associated Press wire, Aamer Madhani) — dateline 30 September 2026, 6:59 AM ET; Exa index timestamp 2026-10-01T07:26:27Z

Iranian officials indicated Wednesday they have received an official U.S. response to Tehran's latest proposal to end the seven-month war, which U.S. President Donald Trump had publicly rejected just days earlier.
The officials did not say what the response contained and whether it was a rejection.
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi presented the U.S. response to President Masoud Pezeshkian at a Cabinet meeting, government spokesperson Fatemeh Mohajerani told the state-run IRNA news agency.
QUOTE (Pezeshkian): "We will make every effort to bring the agreement to fruition and will firmly stand up for the rights of the Iranian people." / "The agreement must now be based on a win-win strategy."
Araghchi last week said he floated the proposal to reopen the strait in a week if the U.S. agreed to lift its blockade of Iranian ports, release frozen Iranian assets and waive sanctions on Iranian oil sales, among other conditions.
QUOTE (Trump, reported): Iran wanted a deal because it was "losing so badly" but its offer "would not be acceptable."
Despite Trump's public rebuff, mediators continued working with Iran and the U.S. to try to broker a deal to end the fighting and open the strait, according to officials not authorised to comment publicly.
Related AP reporting (same wire, carried elsewhere): Araghchi and his delegation were instructed by U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio to leave New York earlier than scheduled, according to two U.S. officials familiar with the decision. The Iranian delegation left New York very early Tuesday.
Also: The U.S. Treasury Department unveiled new sanctions on Tuesday targeting people and companies accused of being financial facilitators or enablers of Iran's military supply chain.
